clue.text: Unable to settle at home, put back bedtime

parts.note: at home means in, as in 'she is in'

indicators.note: put back tells us the word for bed is read backwards

parts.note: bedtime splits as bed plus time; the bed part is turned round and time, abbreviated T, follows it
bedtime splits as bed plus time; the bed part is turned round and time, abbreviated T, follows it

explanation.surface: An insomniac who can't settle down at home pushes back their bedtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unable to settle' looks like restlessness but means unable to pay a bill; 'put back' turns the bed of 'bedtime' into DEB, and its time gives T.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone owing money cannot settle their account, so the two phrases are synonyms.

clue.text: Ten cheers for tiny thing!

parts.note: the figure 10 looks like the letters I and O
ta is British slang for thanks, as is cheers

explanation.surface: Ten cheers raised for something very small.
explanation.walkthrough: Ta and cheers are both casual British ways of saying thanks.
explanation.definitionFit: An iota, the smallest Greek letter, means a very small amount or the slightest bit.

clue.text: Key rings quietly diminish in number

indicators.note: rings means the key's letters encircle the other letter

parts.note: a computer keyboard has a Delete key
p (piano) is the musical marking for quietly

explanation.surface: Keys on a ring dwindle in number as they are lost.
explanation.definitionFit: To deplete is to use up or reduce stocks, making them fewer.

clue.text: Font functions beautifully at first with suitable individual text

indicators.note: at first means only the opening letter of beautifully is used

parts.note: apt means suitable
I, the single person, gives one individual
SMS is the text messaging service, so a text

explanation.surface: A typographer's font that works beautifully with text for each individual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Font' looks typographic but is the church basin for christening.
explanation.definitionFit: Christenings are ceremonies held at the church font, so they are functions of a font.

clue.text: Retired bachelor used to be my doctor

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn, so the past tense for 'used to be' goes back the other way

parts.note: used to be gives the past tense was
my, said of oneself, is one's

explanation.surface: A retired bachelor says he used to be the speaker's doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retired' reverses 'used to be', reaching past 'bachelor'; answer order differs from clue order. 'My' gives one's, the impersonal form.
explanation.definitionFit: Sawbones is old slang for a surgeon or doctor, from the days of amputations.

clue.text: Name state of North American mountain region

indicators.note: state, as in say out loud, signals a word that sounds like the region

parts.note: the Appalachians are a mountain range in eastern North America

explanation.surface: Naming a US state in a mountainous part of North America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'state' looks like a US state but is the verb, to say.
explanation.definitionFit: An appellation is a title or designation, another word for a name.

clue.text: Patient dropping in here unrobed, panicking nurse

indicators.note: to nurse is to hold close, so these words cradle the answer

explanation.surface: A disrobed, panicking patient being tended by a nurse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nurse' looks like the carer but is a verb, to hold.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedridden patient relieves themselves into this receptacle, so what they drop goes in it.

clue.text: Shy queen with very piercing intelligence

indicators.note: piercing means the inner letters go through the middle of the word for intelligence

parts.note: nous is common sense or intelligence
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: A shy queen whose intelligence is very sharp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' only joins the queen and very; nous is British informal for common sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A timid, anxious person is nervous, which matches being shy.

clue.text: Where you might ski round and round and spend a lot

indicators.note: round means the mountain range is turned about

parts.note: the Alps are a skiing destination
a shout, in British pub talk, is one's turn to buy a round of drinks

explanation.surface: A skier circling round and round the slopes at great expense.
explanation.walkthrough: The two 'round's do different jobs: the first is a reversal, the second is British pub slang for a turn to buy drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: To splash out is an idiom for spending money freely or extravagantly.

clue.text: Perhaps more tea and toast made by dog breeders?

definitions.meaning: refills of a cup of tea are an example of these
a toast raised by breeders would be '...!'

explanation.surface: Pouring more tea and raising a glass at a dog breeders' gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition reads the answer as two words, TO PUPS, the sort of toast breeders might drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Refills of a drink, such as another splash of tea in a cup, are called top-ups.

clue.text: Feeling duller at end of term?

definitions.text: Feeling duller at end of term?

parts.words: Feeling duller at end of term?
parts.note: a 'feeling duller' is something that numbs sensation, and the 'end of term' is the close of a pregnancy, at childbirth

explanation.surface: A student feeling more jaded as the school term finishes.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Feeling duller' as a noun, a thing that dulls feeling, and 'term' as the term of a pregnancy.
explanation.definitionFit: This spinal anaesthetic is commonly given to dull pain during labour, which comes when a pregnancy reaches full term.

clue.text: They shock and bestir frail old rebels

indicators.note: rebels as a verb means the letters revolt against their order and regroup

explanation.surface: Elderly rebels who stir themselves into action and shock the establishment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rebels' looks like the people being described, but it is the anagram signal for 'bestir frail old'.
explanation.definitionFit: These medical devices deliver an electric jolt to restart a heart, so they literally administer shocks.

clue.text: Ravel fantasia, arr. Bob Marley?

indicators.note: ravel means tangle, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A Ravel fantasia arranged for reggae star Bob Marley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ravel' poses as the French composer but is the anagram verb; 'arr.' is the music abbreviation for arranged and is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Bob Marley was a famous follower of the Rastafari movement, so he is an example of one.

clue.text: Mother most attentive, keeping temperature steadier

indicators.note: keeping means the phrase holds the word inside its letters

explanation.surface: An attentive mother keeping a feverish child's temperature stable.
explanation.definitionFit: This device switches heating on and off to hold a room's warmth at a set level, steadying it.

clue.text: Hiding bottom in swingers' bar, Arachne cuts odd, discontented figure

indicators.note: hiding bottom means the last letter of the bar is concealed

parts.note: a trapeze is the bar acrobats swing on

indicators.note: cuts means the setter's letter slices into the outer letters
discontented means emptied of contents, keeping only the outer letters

parts.note: Arachne is the setter, who refers to herself as I

explanation.surface: A cryptic image of swingers at a bar and a setter cutting a strange shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hiding bottom' drops the E of TRAPEZE; 'discontented' leaves OD of odd; 'cuts' puts I into it, making OID.
explanation.definitionFit: A trapezoid is a four-sided geometric shape, a figure in the mathematical sense.

clue.text: Ducks surround small lake in city

indicators.note: surround means the ducks' letters go around the others

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of nought, so two ducks are O and O

explanation.surface: Ducks gather round a little lake in a city park.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a duck is a batsman's score of zero, hence O.
explanation.definitionFit: Oslo is the capital city of Norway.

clue.text: During very fine morning yearn to climb tree

indicators.note: to climb in a down clue means the letters are read upwards
During means the yearning comes inside the other pieces

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, the 1 reading as I
to long is to yearn

explanation.surface: On a very fine morning, someone yearning to climb a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 is written with the figure 1 standing for the letter I; the whole assembly AILONGAM is read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The magnolia is a flowering tree or shrub with large showy blooms.

clue.text: Railways regularly neglected, I'm sorry to say

indicators.note: regularly neglected means every other letter is skipped, leaving the even ones

explanation.surface: A sad admission that the railways have been routinely neglected.
explanation.definitionFit: Alas is an exclamation of regret, used just as one says 'unfortunately' or 'sadly'.

clue.text: Father Christmas shedding clothes over one summer month upset part of the WI

indicators.note: over places the stripped name above the rest in this down clue
shedding clothes means the outer letters, its covering, are removed

parts.note: Santa is Father Christmas
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: upset in a down clue turns the month upside down

parts.note: Aug is short for August

explanation.surface: A stripped Santa upsets the Women's Institute in the middle of summer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shedding clothes' takes S and A from SANTA, leaving ANT; 'upset' turns AUG into GUA. WI looks like the Women's Institute, a British women's club, but means the West Indies.
explanation.definitionFit: Antigua is an island in the Caribbean, part of the West Indies.

clue.text: Supporter of an economic system that is disastrous (italics apt)

indicators.note: disastrous signals that the letters are wrecked and rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A capitalist's system declared a disaster, with an aside in brackets.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of capitalism, the free-market economic system, is known by this name.

clue.text: Wrongly say Capone is breaking law

parts.note: ill means wrongly, as in ill-advised
eg, for example, is what 'say' means
Al Capone was the Chicago gangster

explanation.surface: Wrongly claiming that the gangster Capone is breaking the law.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that breaks the law is against it, so the phrase works as an adjective for unlawful.

clue.text: Sex carries advantages for your health

indicators.note: carries means the word for sex supports the advantages above it in this down entry

parts.note: pros are the advantages, as in pros and cons
it is a coy word for sex

explanation.surface: A claim that sex brings benefits to your health.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Your health' is a toast here, not wellbeing.
explanation.definitionFit: Prosit is a German drinking toast meaning 'may it benefit you', said like 'cheers'.

clue.text: Sent certain kingly leaders away, causing amusement

indicators.note: leaders away means the first letter of each of the three words is dropped

explanation.surface: A revolution in which kingly leaders are sent away, to some people's amusement.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing S, C and K from Sent, certain and kingly leaves ENT, ERTAIN and INGLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in a way that amuses or diverts people is doing it entertainingly; the adverb fits the phrase.

clue.text: Excite gentleman, grabbing top of thigh

indicators.note: grabbing means the gentleman's letters seize the other letter

parts.note: sir is the way to address a gentleman

indicators.note: top of in a down clue means the first letter of thigh

explanation.surface: A gentleman getting excited and grabbing at a thigh.
explanation.definitionFit: To stir someone is to rouse or arouse their feelings.

clue.text: Men talk, twitching, of sexual pleasure

parts.note: OR stands for Other Ranks, soldiers who are not officers
gas is idle chatter
a tic is an involuntary twitch

explanation.surface: Men chatting nervously about sex, twitching as they do.
explanation.walkthrough: OR (Other Ranks) is the usual crossword source for 'men'.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes things relating to sexual climax, the height of sexual pleasure.

clue.text: Predicament is easy to bear after heading to pub

indicators.note: after places the word for easy to bear behind the pub's first letter
heading to means take only the opening letter of the word that follows

parts.note: a light load is easy to bear

explanation.surface: A troubled person finding things easier to bear after heading to the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A plight is a difficult or unfortunate situation, a synonym for a predicament.

clue.text: Writing first version of paper, not out wearing women's clothes

indicators.note: wearing means the other letters are dressed in the clothes, which surround them

parts.note: drag is women's clothing worn by a man
FT is the Financial Times newspaper
not out means in, as of a batsman still at the crease

explanation.surface: Someone drafting a paper while dressed, at home, in women's clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not out' is the cricket term for a batsman still in; the FT is the Financial Times newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: To draft something is to write its first rough version, so this is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Whiteness of china egg held in both hands

parts.note: china is rhyming slang for mate (china plate), so a pal

indicators.note: held in means the egg's letter sits between the hands' letters

parts.note: left and right hands give L and R
an egg is O-shaped, so it gives O

explanation.surface: A china egg held carefully in both hands, its pale whiteness admired.
explanation.walkthrough: China = mate is Cockney rhyming slang (china plate rhymes with mate), hence PAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Pallor is an unhealthy paleness of the face, a kind of whiteness.
